span: this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
proposal: A relation between an official traffic-control device and the intersection it controls - equivalently, a region kind for the approach of an intersection together with its connection to that intersection region - so that "intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices" can be read of the very junction the two vehicles entered. The vocabulary relates a device only to the traffic it faces (dev.governs: a lane, approach or region), and relates regions to one another only lane-to-lane (st.lane_connectivity); no atom ties the region a device governs to an intersection region, no atom gives a distance from a device to a region (st.region_geometry measures only from a road user's body outline, dev.position carries a location alone) and no primitive of SS10 computes one. Every reading the vocabulary allows therefore does one of two excluded things. Either it names the intersection region itself as the governed region, which dev.governs' contract excludes outright. Or it substitutes for the approach a region that runs the whole length of the way - st.highway, "the entire public way between its boundary lines", or st.lane, "a longitudinal strip of roadway", both of which continue through every junction of that way - so that a stop sign or signal at any other junction the subject's way passes through exempts this one, which is the approximation the review returned; and st.lane fails a second time, because inside the crossing, where the trigger puts both vehicles, the subject occupies no lane, so the exception would be false exactly when the rule applies and the span would be silently dropped. The span cannot be assumed either: SS9's clause "Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not" governs this category, since the control of an intersection is marked on the road by the very devices SS4 carries as atoms - what is missing is not the category but the relation that attaches those devices to this junction. s6 is an exception span, which rule 3 forbids dropping or narrowing, so the node is withdrawn for the operator to decide the gap.
nearest: dev.governs: "relation: the device applies to a lane, approach or region (which traffic it faces) - Not a stand-in for: a position - the region a device acts on is not where a halt is required and not the intersection region" - the closing words exclude naming the intersection the pair entered as the region the device governs, which is what "intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices" asserts.

st.highway: "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders" - a region that runs the whole length of the way and through every junction on it, so a device governing it is not a device controlling this intersection.

st.lane: "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles - Not a stand-in for: a half of the roadway or a lateral position within a lane" - a lane likewise continues past the junction, and a vehicle inside the crossing, where this rule reads, is on no lane.
st.lane_connectivity: "which lane a lane leads into" - relates one lane to another lane and never a lane or an approach to an intersection region.

dev.position: "location of the device head / sign face - Not a stand-in for: a stop line or a crossing - the distance to a signal head is a different quantity from the distance to the line or region" - a device's location with no relation to, and no distance to, the intersection region.

st.region_geometry: "the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame, and the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it" - the distance it carries is from a road user, never from a device, and it relates no two regions.
decision: the ontology now carries the span: `st.lane_enters` (a lane is an approach to an intersection) with `dev.governs` (the device governs the lane) reads which intersection a device controls

span: upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade,
proposal: | `st.crest` | the point of a roadway at which its longitudinal slope changes from rising to falling in the direction of travel, carried as a region of the road structure with a reference point and a boundary, so that the ground distance from a road user to it is read through `st.region_geometry`; false on a roadway whose profile has no such sign change, and absent on a source that maps no vertical profile **Not a stand-in for:** the slope at a point (`st.grade`), the view a crest restricts (`st.sight_distance`), or a horizontal bend (`st.curvature`) | general |
nearest: st.grade - 'longitudinal slope of the roadway; a crest is its sign change': the contract names the crest but carries only the slope at the point observed, so a read at the road user's own position yields neither the crest's location nor the distance to it, and no primitive of section 10 evaluates an atom at a point offset ahead along the roadway, so 'the approach to or near the crest' cannot be formed from it.

st.sight_distance - 'distance along the road within which another vehicle would be visible from a point': this is what a crest restricts, not where the crest is; reading it for the crest substitutes the consequence for the feature, and it would collide with this same sentence's separate visibility condition, which states its own distance of 500 feet.

st.region_geometry - 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame, and the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it': it supplies exactly the distance this span needs, but only for a structure region the ontology defines, and no region of section 3 denotes a crest.

st.curvature - 'horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point': horizontal, whereas the crest is a vertical feature; the horizontal disjunct of this same sentence is already carried by `drv.road.curved_alignment`, whose contract states that a vertical curve, a grade or a crest is not denoted.
decision: accepted: a crest is a place on the roadway's profile, which the slope at the road user's own position cannot locate for a road user that turns before reaching it; three corpus lines need it (484B.213(2)(a), .407, .603(1))
retired_by: ontology and Core revision 2026-10-05: st.crest, a region kind read through st.region_geometry (ontology/ATOMS.md, Vocab/Ontology/Structure.lean, Vocab/Atoms.lean)

span: where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet.
proposal: | `st.sight_distance` | the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other, from the eye of either driver to the body of the other vehicle at the height convention the source declares: both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there **Not a stand-in for:** whether an actual road user saw, or could see, another at an observation (`rel.visible`), or the clarity of the air (`env.visibility`) | general |
nearest: st.sight_distance - 'distance along the road within which another vehicle would be visible from a point': the view from a point only, so whether a vehicle at that point can be seen by drivers approaching it is not stated

rel.visible - 'b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body, as the source tests it': a relation between road users present at an observation, so it is unknown where no other vehicle is present, while the span asks whether the vehicle could be seen by any vehicle approaching, present or not
decision: accepted as a contract revision, no new atom: the sight distance of a place covers both directions, the view of approaching traffic from that place and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there; what an actual road user saw at an observation stays rel.visible
retired_by: ontology revision 2026-10-06: the st.sight_distance contract, the rel.visible exclusion and the line-of-sight sentence of the mapping guidance (ontology/ATOMS.md, ontology/ATOMS_train.md); Core unchanged
